00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: A Stranger
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Corvus Umbranox appears as the Stranger during the final Thieves Guild scene, before reclaiming his identity as the Gray Fox.
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies the final-scene Stranger as the Gray Fox himself. His reputation as the greatest of thieves and his documented spellcasting support an elite rating, but not the Gray Cowl’s supernatural curse as personal combat power.

0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Abhuki
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Khajiit innkeeper and expert Alteration trainer who directs aspiring masters to Tooth-in-the-Sea.
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her documented expert Alteration training supports advanced magical discipline. Her Mercantile skill is not combat evidence, and she is explicitly unable to perform spells.

0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Name: Achille
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Description: Achille is a Blade stationed at Cloud Ruler Temple, with a basic supported martial profile.
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Blade membership and standard Blades armor support trained martial capability, but the article records no individual feats establishing greater expertise.
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The evidence supports training, but gives little detail about his personal combat proficiency.

02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A veteran Imperial Legion commander who spent forty years in service and devoted much of his career to investigating and disrupting the Dark Brotherhood.
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His decades of service and sustained work against dangerous assassins support a seasoned-combatant rating. The article does not establish elite personal combat mastery or feats warranting a higher tier.

1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida's Bodyguard
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An unnamed Imperial City Watch bodyguard assigned to Adamus Phillida, sworn to protect him if threatened.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His City Watch bodyguard role supports the competent professional-soldier baseline. The article establishes his duty to defend Phillida but no exceptional combat feats.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article does not describe his individual combat training or feats.

01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adanrel
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Description: A poor Waterfront worker with few skills, basic weapons, and limited stealth magic; she is not a Thieves Guild member.
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She explicitly says she lacks the skills for adventuring, and the article describes her as having few skills. Her combat tools support only limited capability.

01681B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adeo
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Seducer captain who leads surviving forces and fights alongside the player against the Forces of Order.
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her captaincy, Dark Seducer arms and standard spells, and direct participation in several battles support seasoned combat capability.

0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adoring Fan
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf commoner and Arena fan who follows the Grand Champion but tends to flee from danger.
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article describes him as a commoner who usually flees peril and almost never uses his dagger, supporting limited practical combat ability.

02F865:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adosi Serethi
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf ostler in Aleswell, affected by Ancotar’s spell and involved in the Zero Visibility quest.
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes an ordinary civilian occupation and no combat-adjacent training or demonstrated capability. The invisibility is imposed by another mage, not her own ability.

016057:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrian Decanius
016057:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner with ordinary civilian status; carries basic armor and weapons, with no documented relevant training or accomplishments.
016057:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Adrian as a commoner. His listed equipment does not establish martial expertise, so ordinary adult basic capability is supported.

02950A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrienne Berene
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adrienne Berene is a scholarly Breton mage whose destructive magic makes her a dangerous opponent, though her documented abilities do not establish exceptional mastery.
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her UESP article describes her as a mage with a particularly powerful Destruction repertoire. That supports a seasoned threat, but no distinctive combat feats or demonstrated mastery justify a higher tier.

068828:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adult Rumare Slaughterfish
068828:Oblivion.esm.Description: A mundane aquatic slaughterfish variant found around Lake Rumare; it is an animal without magical or weapon-wielding abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Its verified form supports an ordinary natural-threat rating; the source establishes no exceptional feats, training, or supernatural abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source confirms the Rumare variant but gives no specific feats for this adult individual.

018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adventurer
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Orc treasure-seeker sent by Gortwog, encountered in Cyrodiil’s ruins and caves; this record is not identified as a unique hero.
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Adventurers actively fight creatures during their expeditions, supporting a competent-combatant baseline. The article establishes no individual feats or exceptional mastery.
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article describes several class variants but does not identify this record’s class; no exceptional individual feats are established.

185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aelwin Merowald
185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Description: An elderly Breton fisherman, injured by a slaughterfish and unable to resume collecting scales.
185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: He says the slaughterfish nearly took his leg and left him too weak to collect the remaining scales, supporting limited capability and vulnerability.

0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aengvir
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf commoner living a simple civilian life in Harlun’s Watch.
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes ordinary civilian life and quest-related dialogue, but no relevant combat, stealth, or practical magical training or accomplishments.

035726:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aenvir
035726:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf former shop employee who repeatedly joined nighttime burglaries and carries a dagger.
035726:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Repeated successful break-ins over several months demonstrate practical theft and infiltration capability, supporting a competent trained-thief tier.
035726:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article gives little evidence of advanced stealth or combat expertise.

098254:Oblivion.esm.Name: Afflicted Brethren
098254:Oblivion.esm.Description: A vampire and former worshipper of Azura, one of five afflicted brethren who slew the powerful vampire Dratik before contracting vampirism.
098254:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor is confirmed as a vampire, and the brethren’s shared history of slaying a powerful vampire supports competent combat capability without establishing exceptional individual mastery.

01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agarmir
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Description: A quest-related Imperial City thief who conceals illicit dealings and prepares a lethal mausoleum ambush.
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His clandestine trade, deceptive cover, secret coordination, and prepared trap followed by a hostile sword attack demonstrate competent dangerous criminal capability, though no evidence supports elite combat or thief mastery.

02D028:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agata
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agata is a Mages Guild Evoker who supports the Leyawiin chapter and helps with its recommendation quest.
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established role as a Guild mage supports competent magical ability, but the article gives no combat feats or combat-specific mastery to justify a higher tier.

0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnar the Unwavering
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord warrior and former Thirsk chieftain who pursued the Uderfrykte Matron; encountered as a corpse at Dive Rock.
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His warrior identity, armor and weapon, and expedition to hunt a dangerous creature support competent trained-fighter/adventurer capability, but not elite mastery.

028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnete the Pickled
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord smith and proprietor of Hammer and Tongs in Skingrad, known for fine armor repair work.
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article supports smithing and repair skill, but no combat training or other dangerous capability; ordinary civilian baseline applies.

037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agronak gro-Malog
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agronak gro-Malog, the Gray Prince, is a vampiric-blooded Orc and long-standing Arena Grand Champion whose unusual abilities make him an exceptionally formidable fighter.
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His nearly decade-long reign and reputation as unbeatable, alongside explicitly heightened abilities from vampiric blood, support elite combat prowess. The evidence does not establish feats warranting legendary mastery.

0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ah-Malz
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ah-Malz is an Argonian blademaster and experienced goblin hunter who regularly spars with a fellow Fighters Guild member.
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His blademaster identity, expert goblin hunting, and regular sparring support a seasoned-combatant rating, but the article establishes no exceptional feats warranting an elite tier.

034E87:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahdarji
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ahdarji is a retired Thieves Guild thief and advanced Light Armor trainer who uses a stolen ring to gather and sell information.
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established thief and information-gathering experience, together with advanced Light Armor training, supports seasoned professional capability. The evidence does not establish exceptional mastery.
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her former theft accomplishments are described only broadly; exceptional mastery is not established.

0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahjazda
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: A peaceful Khajiit shopkeeper who relies on her fists if threatened and cannot cast spells.
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article describes her as peaceful, unarmed, and dependent on fists in a fight; her enchanter class does not translate into spellcasting ability.

0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ajum-Kajin
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Argonian mage and high-ranking Blackwood Company member who uses mage spells in combat.
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His mage identity and combat use of spells support basic trained magical capability; his rank and guards do not establish greater personal power.

01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Akaviri Commander Mishaxhi
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Description: A ghostly Tsaesci commander and renowned Akaviri tactician guarding the Draconian Madstone at Fort Pale Pass.
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Identified as one of the Akaviri invasion’s greatest tacticians; he remains armed and guards the fort. This supports highly accomplished military and martial expertise, not legendary individual combat.
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His strategic reputation is explicit, but specific personal combat feats are limited; the tier reflects command and martial expertise, not mastery of every warrior skill.

03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alawen
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alawen is a Wood Elf master marksman who hunts with a bow and trains others in Marksman.
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established mastery as a Marksman trainer supports the project's Master combat trainer baseline. The claim that she is Cyrodiil's best shot is only reported as a rumor and is not needed for this tier.

0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alberic Litte
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Mages Guild associate with broad low-level spell use and advanced Conjuration training services.
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His personal repertoire is described as low-level spells across the schools, supporting basic practical magical capability; offering advanced Conjuration training adds evidence of relevant discipline.

0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aldos Othran
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A grieving farmer whose drinking and limited armed resistance end in a scripted death during the Cheydinhal corruption quest.
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: He carries an iron dagger and initiates a fight, but the account describes no relevant training or expertise; he quickly dies to the guard.

00A110:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aleron Loche
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Description: Aleron Loche is a commoner caught in Kurdan’s deadly hunt; he says he cannot fight and has never held a weapon.
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His dialogue directly establishes inexperience and lack of weapon training. No combat-adjacent ability is evidenced.

01D346:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alessia Ottus
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial civilian author of city guidebooks, with no evidenced combat or combat-adjacent training.
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP biography identifies her as a commoner and describes writing, worship, and ordinary routines, but no relevant practical ability.

035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alga
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord bard and storyteller who teaches basic Speechcraft and can use bard spells.
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her demonstrated bard magic provides combat-adjacent capability; her storytelling and basic Speechcraft training alone do not establish advanced expertise.

01D344:Oblivion.esm.Name: Algot the Northerner
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord bard and Imperial City civilian who does odd jobs and some adventuring; no notable combat training or feats are established.
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article mentions only a little adventuring, with no evidence of professional training or exceptional ability. The project's ordinary adult civilian baseline applies.

18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alix Lencolia
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Young Breton crusader and master Blade trainer, renowned for his sword skill and associated with the Blade Training quest.
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Alix as the master trainer in Blade and records other trainers calling him famous for his skill with a blade. Established mastery in a combat discipline supports Tier 6.

08595D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alonzo
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alonzo is a Redguard bandit boss who leads raids on travelers with members of the Black Bow Bandits.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His active role in bandit raids supports competent combat capability, but the article provides no evidence of veteran training or exceptional personal feats.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source establishes his bandit role but does not describe his individual combat skill.

031867:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aloys Bincal
031867:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial farmer and settler who takes refuge from nearby goblins and later helps establish Cropsford.
031867:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes him as an ordinary farmer, with no demonstrated combat, stealth, or magical training; his fear of goblins does not establish adventuring capability.

01207B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Althel's Ghost
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cursed ghost of Althel, a Vitharn scout and archer who detected the invaders and defended the gate.
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her patrol and early warning, defensive archer role, and demonstrated ability to hit targets support competent trained scout capability, without evidence of elite mastery.

030196:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alval Uvani
030196:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dark Elf battlemage and master of Destruction magic, Alval is a dangerous opponent with additional Mysticism and Restoration spells.
030196:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article identifies him as a master of Destruction and describes him as a formidable opponent. That established magical mastery supports Tier 6; his quest role alone does not raise the tier.

02D027:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alves Uvenim
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf alchemist and Mages Guild journeyman; a practiced researcher who advises Rosentia, with no established combat feats or combat specialization.
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her documented expertise is alchemy and research, not combat. The ordinary-adult baseline is appropriate absent evidence of combat training or demonstrated fighting ability.

08209B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alyssa
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dead Breton conjurer found after a disabling leg fracture; no practical magical or combat feats are documented.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her conjurer identity warrants assessing magical capability, but the article establishes no demonstrated spellcraft. The represented encounter is her corpse, incapacitated by injury.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her past magical proficiency is unspecified; this tier reflects the documented corpse encounter form.

0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amantius Allectus
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and writer whose documented activities center on scholarship and private plant experiments.
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP establishes no combat training, practical adventuring discipline, or demonstrated dangerous capability; ordinary adult baseline applies.

028E75:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ambroise Canne
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Description: A renowned Block specialist whose advanced instruction and local reputation establish him as a highly accomplished defensive combatant.
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies Ambroise as an advanced Block trainer and reports that townspeople regard his shield skill as superior to the Fighters Guild trainer’s. This supports an elite specialist rating, but not master-level combat mastery.

01207A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amiable Fanriene
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amiable Fanriene is a highly capable Breton conjurer whose formidable spellcasting contrasts with his persistent paranoia.
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article describes him as one of the Isles’ most capable mages and details a broad repertoire of powerful spells, supporting a master-level assessment.

026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amir
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Description: A named Redguard assassin and worshipper of Molag Bal, armed with a shortsword and dagger.
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Amir as an assassin, supporting trained capability in a relevant discipline; no specific exceptional feats or demonstrated mastery are described.

03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amkaos
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amkaos is a hostile Dremora torturer and patrol guard in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise, equipped for combat.
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His hostile guard role, Dremora armor and longsword, and intrinsic resistance to magic support seasoned combat capability.

0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amminus Gregori
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cheydinhal City Guard assigned to watch an Oblivion Gate; equipped with guard armor and a silver longsword.
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His guard duty, martial equipment, and knight-class identity support competent trained-fighter capability, but the evidence does not establish seasoned or elite expertise.

000F62:Knights.esp.Name: Amragor
000F62:Knights.esp.Description: A Wood Elf healer in the reconditioned Chapel of Dibella who knows healer spells and an additional Restoration spell.
000F62:Knights.esp.Reason: His healer identity and known Restoration magic support trained, practical magical capability, but the evidence does not establish advanced mastery.

03563B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amusei
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Argonian freelance thief who later earns a Thieves Guild career and serves as a messenger for the Gray Fox.
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Thievery is his profession, but early failures—including botching the Guild-entry race, getting jailed after stealing a ring, and being caught stealing food—show limited execution. His later Guild advancement and trusted message-running support competent professional capability, not exceptional mastery.

05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anaxes
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anaxes is a Xivilai lord encountered in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise, where the inhabitants have trapped him in his cave.
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article confirms his Xivilai form. The project baseline assigns verified Xivilai tier 6; unique feats are not required.

0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancestor Guardian
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Description: A guardian summoned through the Dunmer Ancestor Guardian ability; its exact creature form is not established by the available evidence.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Manual deleveling review: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Initial balance assignment; editable after in-game testing.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.

05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Ghost
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable ghost variant that attacks with frost-focused magic and is described as more dangerous than a standard ghost.
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified ancient form is explicitly more formidable than the ordinary ghost baseline (tier 3), supporting a modest increase to seasoned threat.

070913:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Sanctified Dead
070913:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable spectral variant that relies on magical attacks, particularly frost, and is more powerful than a standard ghost.
070913:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor’s identity matches the ancient ghost form. UESP describes ancient ghosts as more formidable than standard ghosts, with more powerful spells, supporting a step above the project’s ordinary ghost baseline.

02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancotar
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Mages Guild wizard and warlock whose magical research made people and creatures across a wide area invisible; he also developed a counterspell.
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His demonstrated area-effect spellcraft and ability to devise a counterspell establish substantial magical competence. The evidence supports a seasoned mage, but not exceptional combat mastery.

01D354:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancus Afranius
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Description: Breton bard and Thieves Guild member who uses bard spells in combat, but has no documented exceptional feats or advanced proficiency.
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His combat use of bard spells supports novice-level practical magical capability. Thieves Guild membership alone does not establish advanced stealth or theft expertise.

00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andragil
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf Bravil resident and master Block trainer who tests trainees by striking them with a warhammer.
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Andragil is explicitly identified as a master trainer in Block, a combat discipline. Other expert trainers credit her instruction, and her training test demonstrates her ability to withstand a prolonged combat challenge.

0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andre Labouche
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Named Breton spellsword found dead at Dive Rock; his note and corpse point to The Horror of Dive Rock.
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His in-life spellsword identity and supported spell use indicate basic magical training, but no advanced proficiency or combat accomplishments are established.
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article gives limited evidence of his practical proficiency; the encounter form is a corpse.

030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andreas Draconis
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial publican and Dark Brotherhood quest target; no established combat-adjacent training or accomplishments.
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article identifies him as an innkeeper who sells food and rents beds. His threat to fight when confronted shows willingness, not demonstrated expertise; ordinary adult baseline applies.

07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Androcide
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Unverified creature encounter; no actor-specific UESP evidence establishes its form or capabilities.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied record identifies a creature but not its species or lore. Without a verified form, no project baseline can be applied.

026B36:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anedhel
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf witch and Clavicus Vile worshipper who knows witch spells, including Destruction and Mysticism magic.
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her witch identity and known practical magic support an apprentice-level magical capability; no greater proficiency or accomplishments are established.
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The evidence establishes spell use but not the extent of her magical training.

0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalmo
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: High Elf alchemist and Mages Guild Evoker who offers basic Mysticism training; no combat feats or combat-focused expertise are established.
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Angalmo as an adult mortal but establishes no combat training or demonstrated fighting ability. Basic Mysticism training does not establish combat mastery, so the ordinary adult baseline is appropriate.

026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalsama
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Description: A High Elf mage and Sheogorath worshipper whose life centers on the shrine; she knows mage spells but has no documented advanced feats.
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her identification as a mage and knowledge of spells support basic apprentice-level magical capability, but the evidence establishes no greater practical expertise.

01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angelie
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Redguard commoner living a quiet, ordinary life in the Imperial City.
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified biography establishes no combat or combat-adjacent training or accomplishments; her Commoner identity supports the ordinary adult baseline.

052F61:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anglor's Ghost
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anglor’s ghost is a cursed Wood Elf conjurer whose past magical support is noted, though the ghost cannot cast spells in the encounter.
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His conjurer identity and reported sacrifice of his Magicka to restore Prior Dreth’s support a modest trained-mage tier; no stronger practical ability is established.

00A299:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anguilon
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf pirate in Anvil who carries an iron dagger and keeps to the dockside inns.
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Pirate identity and dagger support basic dangerous-world capability, but the article provides no evidence of advanced combat or combat-adjacent training.

0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antoine Branck
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Breton stablehand who tends horses and scouts the Green Road for customers.
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes ordinary stable work and an iron war axe, but no relevant advanced training or demonstrated dangerous capability.

023E36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her assassin role, regular sneak-mode training, and reference to kills support trained but still developing covert capability; no elite feats are established.

034E72:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brodras
034E72:Oblivion.esm.Description: Brodras is a Wood Elf Fighters Guild associate, Heavy Armor trainer, and crusader who regularly spars with a fellow guildmember.
034E72:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Fighters Guild role, regular sparring, and combat training support a competent-fighter baseline. His training is described as basic, with no evidence of mastery or exceptional feats.

00A085:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brokil gro-Shatur
00A085:Oblivion.esm.Description: Orc commoner and inn patron whose routine centers on socializing and drinking.
00A085:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified biography establishes an ordinary civilian life but no relevant combat, stealth, or magical training; basic adult capability is the supported baseline.

0477DB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bronsila Kvinchal

0477DB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Evidence establishes ordinary civilian work and no relevant combat, stealth, or magical training; assign the basic adult baseline.

02991E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brotch Calus
02991E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Retired Imperial alchemist in Bruma who provides advanced Alchemy training and directs advanced students to Sinderion.
02991E:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His advanced-trainer role, reputation as an accomplished alchemist, and referral of less advanced students establish highly accomplished professional expertise in Alchemy. Sinderion is explicitly described as more knowledgeable.

0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Hjar
0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Description: A quiet Nord Moth caretaker whose documented routine centers on prayer and temple life.
0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP evidence establishes no combat, stealth, or practical magical training; monk identity alone does not demonstrate those capabilities.

0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Holger
0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A peaceful Ancestor Moth caretaker who can reveal the catacombs and escort the player to unlock a door.
0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The evidence supports ordinary adult capability and a quest-support role, but establishes no relevant combat, stealth, or magical training.

0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Hridi
0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord Moth Caretaker at the Temple of the Ancestor Moths; maintains crops and harvests silk.
0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article supports ordinary caretaking and farming, but no demonstrated combat, stealth, or practical magical expertise. Monk identity alone does not establish mastery.

033907:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Martin
033907:Oblivion.esm.Description: Brother Martin is a former practitioner of Daedric magic and a capable ritual scholar who later serves as a priest.
033907:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His dangerous youthful studies and successful deciphering and performance of the Mysterium Xarxes ritual establish highly accomplished Daedric scholarship and ritual expertise. His Akatosh avatar is a separate divine transformation, not evidence that his ordinary Conjurer form has comparable power.
033907:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His past practice is described as youthful and abandoned; the article does not establish that he remains a master of combat magic.

035EAC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes ordinary innkeeping and limited quest assistance, but no relevant combat, magical, stealth, or other dangerous training.

00A08D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Olava the Fair

034E7C:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His stealth-instructor role does not establish combat mastery, and the article provides no combat feats. Basic is a cautious baseline for an adult mortal without established combat training.

090AB3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her actor-specific article identifies her as a master trainer in Restoration and describes her as an exceptionally gifted healer, supporting the Master tier.

035EB5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Olfand

035EB5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Smithing and commerce do not establish combat capability. His basic Light Armor instruction supports ordinary trained familiarity, but not advanced expertise or demonstrated adventuring ability.

026B4D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Olyn Seran

026B4D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Actor-specific dialogue identifies Olyn as a powerful conjurer, and his master-trainer role supports rare magical mastery. The evidence supports tier 6, but not a higher tier.

033906:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article describes advisory duties and routine castle access, but no feats in stealth, theft, security, infiltration, evasion, or assassination. Basic civilian capability is supported.

035ECA:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ongar the World-Weary
035ECA:Oblivion.esm.Description: Retired Thieves Guild member who now fences stolen goods in Bruma.
035ECA:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His fencing role and occasional sneaking for food suggest limited criminal familiarity, but the article establishes no advanced theft, infiltration, or combat expertise.

01CF33:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ontus Vanin

01CF33:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Forty years at the Arcane University, battlemage identity, and knowledge of battlemage spells support seasoned magical capability, though no exceptional feats are documented.

011F9E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Orc Adventurer Captain

0222B9:Oblivion.esm.Name: Orgnolf Hairy-Legs
0222B9:Oblivion.esm.Description: A castle porter and commoner involved as a suspect in the Canvas the Castle investigation.
0222B9:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article establishes ordinary porter duties and drinking habits, but no relevant combat training, adventuring feats, or practical combat-adjacent expertise.

02D022:Oblivion.esm.Name: Orintur

0293E4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Parwen

0A3164:Oblivion.esm.Name: Pelagius
0A3164:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial Blade and regular sparring partner at Cloud Ruler Temple.

015D7F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Penniless Olvus

015D7F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP describes his combat resources as limited and provides no evidence of relevant training or advanced capability.

01D356:Oblivion.esm.Name: Pennus Mallius

030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Perennia Draconis
030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Elderly Imperial farmer at Applewatch; she attacks if threatened during the Dark Brotherhood quest Next of Kin.
030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her biography supports ordinary farming, not combat or combat-adjacent training. Her age, easily rattled nerves, and defensive reaction support limited capability.
